maya: Hey team — I'm Maya (new runtime dev). Trying to build from source on my machine (Ubuntu 22.04) and hit a link error during make. Can someone point me to the usual debug steps?

devon: welcome! Can you paste the error and what CUDA/toolkit you have installed?

maya: Here's the tail of the build log:

```
/usr/bin/ld: libruntime.so: undefined reference to `cublasCreate_v2'
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
make[2]: *** [runtime/bin/worker] Error 1
```

maya: I'm using CUDA 12.2 installed via apt (libcudnn from local tar), nvcc reports 12.2, nvidia-driver is 535.86.10 according to nvidia-smi.

devon: two quick checks: 1) is your LD_LIBRARY_PATH pointing to the same cuda libs used at link time? 2) are you building inside a container where /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so comes from the host and may be incompatible?

chris: also check which cublas your CMake finds. run `ldd build/runtime/bin/worker | grep cublas` and `grep -R CUBLAS /path/to/cmake/cache` — sometimes the pkgconfig picks system headers but a different runtime lib.

maya: ldd shows:

```
libcublas.so.12 => not found
```

maya: but /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64/libcublas.so exists

devon: sounds like the rpath wasn't set. Either export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64 before running, or add -Wl,-rpath,/usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64 to the linker flags in CMake.

maya: trying that... also building inside Docker (dev image from infra). infra-bot: container info?

infra-bot: Container image: redwood/dev-runtime:2026-03-01 (glad to help). Host driver: 535.86.10. Note: image ships with CUDA headers only; it expects libcuda from host via GPU mount.

chris: if the container lacks the matching libcublas, you need to bind-mount host /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64 or use the runtime image that includes cuda runtime libs. We usually recommend using our gpu-dev image: redwood/gpu-dev-12.2 which bundles matching libs.

maya: mounted host /usr/local/cuda-12.2/lib64 and re-ran make; new error during runtime:

```
terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::runtime_error'
  what():  cudaErrorNoKernelImageForDevice: no kernel image is available for execution on the device
Aborted (core dumped)
```

devon: that means the PTX/arch you're compiling for doesn't match the GPU. What's the GPU model? `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=name,compute_cap --format=csv`

maya: host is A100-SXM4-80GB, compute capability 8.0

chris: check your nvcc flags: make sure -gencode / -arch include sm_80 or provide ptx fallback. Our BUILD.md recommends `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80 -gencode=arch=compute_80,code=compute_80` for A100.

maya: fixed the nvcc flags in the CMake toolchain file, rebuild succeeded. Thanks for the quick help! :tada:

devon: awesome — welcome aboard. Add a short note to the onboarding doc about dev image mismatch and rpath if you have a minute.

maya: will do, linking the PR here when ready.

chris: ping me for a quick walkthrough on the build flags later today.

maya: thanks everyone!
